blocks.text: This page tracks the Richmond MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for September 2026: $1,015,800 for a typical home, down 6.8% over twelve months.
Richmond benchmark prices and trends, September 2026

A typical Richmond home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $1,015,800 in September 2026. That is little changed at −0.9% on the month, little changed at −1.4% over three months, down 4.0% over six months and down 6.8% over the year. Over three years it is down 13.7%, and over five years down 2.7%.
The weakest one-year move in Richmond was for an apartment homes at −9.1%; the strongest was a townhouse at −2.3%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,871,100) and an apartment ($635,600) is $1,235,500, and a townhouse ($1,025,000) sits $389,400 above the apartment benchmark.
Against Greater Vancouver, where the all-home benchmark was $1,075,900, Richmond is 5.6% below. Over the year Greater Vancouver moved down 5.5% against down 6.8% here.
Of the 20 areas this board reports, Richmond ranks 10 by all-home benchmark, with Ladner above it at $1,033,700 and Port Moody below it at $1,011,500.

Detached homes in Richmond: benchmark $1,871,100, down 2.8% in a month, down 3.2% in three months, down 5.2% in six months, down 8.5% in a year, down 14.3% in three years and down 5.2% in five. That is 4.8% above the detached benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,784,700).

Townhouse homes in Richmond: benchmark $1,025,000, little changed at +0.3% in a month, little changed at +0.0% in three months, little changed at −1.2% in six months, down 2.3% in a year, down 10.1% in three years and up 8.2% in five. That is 0.8% above the townhouse benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,016,700).

Apartment homes in Richmond: benchmark $635,600, little changed at +0.4% in a month, down 2.1% in three months, down 5.8% in six months, down 9.1% in a year, down 14.0% in three years and up 1.6% in five. That is 6.9% below the apartment benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($682,500).

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Richmond?
faq.a: In September 2026, a typical Richmond home was $1,015,800, with detached at $1,871,100.

faq.q: Are Richmond home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: Richmond is down 6.8% over twelve months and little changed at −1.4% over three months.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: How do I find out what my home is worth?
faq.a: Jared prepares a home evaluation from recent comparable sales and the condition of your home. Contact him on 604-928-1361 or through the form on this site to arrange one.
